verdict.rationale: Gitea is a free, MIT-licensed, self-hosted Git service offering 'full control.' Its data lives in Git repositories and in standard databases the user runs (SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL, etc.), which implicitly keeps data in open, portable stores. However, the evidence documents no first-party export or dump feature covering issues, PRs, wikis, packages and other data. A community question about backup and restore is only a question, not concrete contradiction. missing for 10: a documented export/dump feature for all data (issues, PRs, users, packages), explicit open-format export documentation, and hands-on corroboration of a full exit or migration out of Gitea.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: Free, self-hosted Git service under the MIT license. Full control, unlimited users and repositories.
Offers seamless integration with leading databases, including SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL, TiDB, and MS SQL.
